UnitStatement: The product is the Chirality desktop harness and bundled agent operating system.
The primary repository/workspace for Chirality is chirality-app-dev.
The development source path is chirality/projects/chirality-app-dev/frontend in the complete source tree, and frontend/ in the reviewed archive snapshot.
The public release snapshot path is chirality-app/frontend, maintained as a release operation rather than the active vNext development source.
Status: Revised product requirements after repository, execution-plan, frontend, and harness-runtime assessment.
Source basis includes Chirality App product descriptions from conversations with the developer.
Source basis includes the existing frontend/ files.

Source basis includes Anthropic Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code SDK documentation current as of 2026-05-20, covering query() options, permissions, hooks, MCP, sessions, SessionStore, system prompts, subagents, and hosting guidance for the first concrete adapter.
Source basis includes SCA-APP-001 Provider-General Runtime and Pi Pattern-Corpus Reorientation, accepted on 2026-06-13.
Chirality is a desktop harness for running governed AI agents against a user-selected local filesystem workspace.
Chirality packages a release-managed instruction root inside the desktop app and keeps mutable project execution state in a user-selected working root (projectRoot).
The product exists to accelerate deliverable-heavy professional work while preserving human authority, provenance, auditability, and filesystem-native state.
Outputs remain drafts or decision support until accepted by an accountable human.
Core product thesis: project truth lives in git-tracked plain files; if a decision is not in a versioned file, it does not exist for purposes of reliance.
Runtime thesis: agents propose and organize, the runtime records what happened, deterministic tools validate and transform, humans decide what can be relied upon, and git-tracked files remember.
Chirality should use a provider-adapter architecture where external provider SDKs and APIs remain implementation substrates behind Chirality-owned contracts.
The Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic remains the first concrete adapter and the current shipped path.

Chirality should not reimplement generic primitives the current adapter provides well (model/tool loop, built-in file tools, bash surface, permission-mode machinery, hook dispatch, MCP transport, SDK session transcripts, subagent invocation, compaction messages) when they can be governed by Chirality-owned policy.
Chirality must treat every provider/SDK as a replaceable engine behind product-owned contracts, not as the product runtime contract itself.

Chirality owns the product-critical governance shell: instruction-root vs working-root separation, persona/system-prompt composition, working-root validation, professional-boundary posture, _STATUS.md lifecycle authority, Dependencies.csv contract behavior, subagent governance allowlists, path containment, instruction-root write blocking, runtime redaction, provenance events, UI transport compatibility, local packaging, the Chirality audit mirror, and adapter-replacement fallback criteria.

The vNext runtime is provider-adapter-general, contract-owned, and Chirality-governed: adapters supply reusable machinery only where verified while Chirality defines reliance boundaries, configures the engine, records what happened, and preserves governed exit paths.

The desktop and harness shell are substantially scaffolded: typed API routes, JSON session records, attachment validation, provider selection, subagent governance, network guardrails, API-key handling, UI surfaces, and Section 8 validation exist.

The harness is not yet a full governed agent runtime; it is mostly a provider streaming adapter where opts.tools is not backed by a real tool surface, permission behavior is partly simulated, there is no append-only per-turn Chirality transcript, and the Next.js turn route owns too much runtime lifecycle.
The next development objective is to evolve the shell into a governed provider-adapter Chirality runtime without becoming a thin Claude Code wrapper or any other external harness wrapper.

The first implementation slice must establish a thin TurnEngine wrapper around the first adapter, adapter option construction, provider/SDK-message mapping, append-only Chirality session events, redacted run logging, first-adapter settings isolation, prompt composition, and an explicit AgentEnginePort/RuntimeEngineContract boundary without changing the browser-facing SSE contract.

Local tool exposure should begin by configuring first-adapter SDK built-ins and in-process Chirality MCP tools behind capability-forward policy with explicit hard-deny precedence, not by building a custom model/tool loop from scratch.

R0/R1 must create a reliance-boundary register identifying which product-critical semantics are enforced by Chirality code, adapter configuration, adapter hooks/callbacks, or prompt text; product-critical safety or audit semantics may not depend on prompt text or opaque provider/SDK defaults alone.

A custom runtime remains an explicit fallback if the R0/R1 first-adapter probe proves the adapter cannot satisfy, expose, or be wrapped to satisfy a product-critical Chirality requirement without weakening governance.
Goal: provide a local desktop application that runs agent workflows against a selected working root without requiring an external database.
Goal: preserve strict separation between bundled instruction root and mutable working root.
Goal: make agent work auditable through plain files, git diffs, lifecycle files, dependency registers, immutable snapshots, and runtime session events.
Goal: provide matrix-based navigation into two execution surfaces - WORKBENCH for interactive persona agents and PIPELINE for operative task categories.
Goal: support streaming chat turns with session persistence, runtime options, interrupts, multimodal attachments, and current Anthropic provider integration.
Goal: enforce safety and governance boundaries - human authority at gates, no automated issuance, no hidden project memory, fail-closed subagent delegation, and explicit outbound network policy.
Goal: provide deterministic tools and validation workflows for scaffolding, schema checks, dependency closure, harness runtime validation, and release packaging.
Goal: ship a macOS 15+ Apple Silicon unsigned DMG build path with instruction-root integrity verification.
Goal: build a provider-adapter runtime architecture while keeping Chirality-specific governance in product-owned code.

Goal: put every provider/SDK behind a product-owned AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract so public APIs, canonical event schema, session storage, permission semantics, and governance rules are not provider-shaped.
Goal: maintain engine conformance tests that verify the Chirality runtime contract independently of the specific provider/SDK adapter.
Goal: establish a thin TurnEngine that owns the harness turn lifecycle outside the HTTP route and delegates model/tool execution to the first adapter through the engine contract.

Goal: persist accepted user input before adapter execution and persist success, failure, interruption, permission, hook, tool, compaction, and subagent lifecycle records in an append-only Chirality event log.
Goal: compose real prompt/system context from instruction-root governance, active persona, project-root boundaries, mode policy, and configured tool surface.
Goal: configure adapter options deterministically - model, cwd, permission mode, allowed/disallowed tools, hooks, MCP servers, subagents, session ID/resume, settings isolation, and system prompt.

Goal: implement a Chirality capability policy / permission overlay using adapter permission modes, explicit hard-deny precedence, disallowedTools, hooks, and canUseTool; never treat allowedTools alone as a restriction boundary.
Goal: prefer in-process Chirality MCP tools for _STATUS.md, Dependencies.csv, scope scan, scaffold, and future deterministic Chirality adapters.
Goal: keep the canonical Chirality audit mirror under .chirality/sessions/<id>/ even when the SDK writes or mirrors its own richer transcripts.
Goal: store SDK session linkage (sdkSessionId, project key, transcript location or store key) in Chirality session metadata.
Goal: treat SDK subagents as governed runtime entities with Chirality identity, parent-child linkage, restricted capabilities, and stored output artifacts.
Goal: preserve a future path for generic Domain Engine Profiles only after the core governed SDK runtime is stable.
Goal: use OpenPipeStress, if adopted, as the first concrete Domain Engine Profile fixture rather than as Chirality core behavior.
Non-goal: the product must not replace professional judgment or produce binding approval records autonomously.
Non-goal: the product must not sign, seal, certify, approve, issue, transmit, or otherwise release professional work for reliance.
Non-goal: the product must not make safety-critical decisions without human review.
Non-goal: the product must not conduct financial transactions or binding commitments.
Non-goal: the product must not depend on an external project database.
Non-goal: the product must not persist project truth in hidden app state, chats, caches, or vendor systems.
Non-goal: the product must not treat local UI preferences, API keys, runtime logs, SDK transcripts, or chat drafts as authoritative project state.
Non-goal: the product must not allow outbound network access beyond the current shipped Anthropic API path unless a governed future implementation tranche explicitly permits it.
Non-goal: the product must not treat prompt instructions as the only safety boundary for filesystem writes or tool execution.
Non-goal: the product must not add bash as a user-enabled capability before permission, hooks, result storage, timeout, audit logging, and packaging checks exist.

Non-goal: the product must not add remote MCP servers, plugins, remote execution, or a plugin marketplace before local/in-process SDK integration, permission policy, hooks, event logging, and result storage are stable.
Non-goal: the product must not reimplement provider/SDK-provided primitives when the current adapter satisfies requirements and can be governed by Chirality overlays.

Non-goal: the product must not collapse into a thin Claude Code, Pi, or other external wrapper where provider defaults, transcript shape, tool names, or external assumptions define Chirality runtime semantics.
Non-goal: the product must not chase feature parity with Claude Code CLI, Pi, or any external codebase; provider SDKs are implementation substrates, not product identity or governance authority.
Non-goal: the product must not use Claude Code branding, visual identity, or user-facing copy that makes Chirality appear to be Claude Code or an Anthropic product.
Non-goal: the product must not load ambient user/global Claude Code settings (~/.claude/settings.json) or local .claude/settings.local.json in shipped builds.

Non-goal: the product must not use bypassPermissions in shipped builds or ordinary operator workflows; any developer-only bypass stays guarded by explicit local configuration and Chirality deny hooks.

Non-goal: the product must not import Pi packages, fork Pi, build a Pi adapter, introduce a Node 22 Pi sidecar, raise the runtime floor for Pi, or run a Pi spike under current scope; Pi is a pattern corpus/reference only after SCA-APP-001.
Non-goal: the product must not implement concrete non-Anthropic providers under the strategic provider-adapter ruling without a bounded future implementation tranche.

Non-goal: the product must not reopen retired execution-scope items such as unified pipeline run records, dependency graph generation, deliverable locks, or staleness tooling without a governed scope amendment; harness session event logs do not by themselves reactivate retired pipeline deliverables.
Non-goal: the product must not become OpenPipeStress, a pipe-stress solver, or any other domain-specific engineering solver.
Non-goal: the product must not allow agents to write directly into protected domain-engine model paths.

The Professional Operator is a licensed professional, project lead, or accountable reviewer who needs AI-assisted production while retaining decision rights; they select the working root, approve gates, review evidence, and decide what can be relied upon.

The Project Orchestrator converts a scope of work into packages, deliverables, lifecycle records, document kits, dependency registers, and coordination artifacts using ORCHESTRATOR, WORKING_ITEMS, RECONCILIATION, CHANGE, and PIPELINE lanes.
The Specialist Contributor is a user or workflow that executes bounded deliverable-local work through TASK, DEPENDENCIES, CHIRALITY_FRAMEWORK, CHIRALITY_LENS, ESTIMATING, or audit agents.

The Governance Maintainer is responsible for agent instruction conformance, invariant consistency, deterministic tooling, permission modes, runtime policies, and release-managed instruction root changes.
The Release Operator builds, validates, packages, verifies instruction-root inclusion, and distributes local unsigned desktop builds.
The Harness Runtime Maintainer is responsible for TurnEngine, event schema, tool contracts, permission policy, provider adapters, result storage, context compaction, and validation evolution.

The Future Domain Engine Integrator defines Domain Engine Profiles, deterministic adapters, protected path rules, manifest requirements, and operation-proposal workflows; this role appears only after the harness runtime spine, permissions, tools, hooks, and result storage are stable.

The Future Domain Reviewer is an accountable reviewer who examines domain-engine proposals, deterministic results, provenance, and professional-boundary notices before any accepted domain state changes.
Principle: filesystem is the database - project state is represented as human-readable files under the working root.
Principle: git is the event store for project truth - review, audit, rollback, and approvals bind to git-tracked content.
Principle: runtime events are an audit trail, not project truth; session logs explain what happened but gate-relevant decisions must still land in versioned project files.
Principle: human authority at every gate - agents propose; humans approve, issue, sign, seal, and decide.
Principle: evidence over plausibility - claims require provenance, and unknowns become TBD, not guesses.
Principle: no hidden memory for project truth - runtime convenience state is allowed only when explicitly non-authoritative.
Principle: instruction root and working root are separate - release-managed agent OS files must not be modified by project execution.
Principle: provider-adapter-general, contract-owned - provider SDKs may supply generic agent-loop mechanics, but Chirality owns the runtime contract exposed to the app and to project governance.

Principle: reliance boundaries are first-class - audit, permission, lifecycle, filesystem-truth, transcript-canonicality, and human-gate semantics must be defined and tested in Chirality terms, not inferred from provider/SDK defaults.
Principle: engine replaceability by construction - every adapter must sit behind explicit contracts, conformance tests, and fallback criteria so upstream changes do not silently redefine the product.
Principle: SDK isolation - shipped builds must not load ambient user/global Claude Code settings; programmatic options and Chirality instruction-root policy are the source of runtime behavior.

Principle: provider-neutral core - core runtime records, APIs, and tests use Chirality terms; Claude/SDK-specific identifiers, message names, transcript paths, permission modes, and tool names are translated at the adapter boundary.
Principle: routes stay thin - HTTP routes parse requests, handle transport, acquire/release locks, and forward events, while runtime services own behavior.
Principle: persist accepted user input early - a killed or interrupted process must leave a recoverable accepted-turn record.
Principle: separate UI events from runtime events - browser UIEvents remain stable and compact while persisted runtime events may be richer and versioned.
Principle: expose only policy-permitted capabilities to the model - tool-surface resolution happens before adapter request construction, and allowedTools alone is not enough.

Principle: hard denies override allows - provider/SDK deny rules, hook denials, path-containment failures, protected-path rules, release/professional boundaries, and governance denials override any allow decision.
Principle: safety lives in runtime code - prompts reinforce safety but do not replace path containment, permission policy, hooks, result budgets, timeouts, and packaging/network controls.
Principle: MCP is a transport, not a bypass - in-process Chirality MCP tools must pass through the same permission, hook, path, redaction, and event-logging policy as SDK built-ins.
Principle: product identity stays Chirality - SDK usage must not make the app look, behave, or describe itself as Claude Code.
Principle: immutable snapshots - snapshot-producing runs create timestamped folders that are not overwritten, though _LATEST.md pointers may move.
Principle: least structure that works - rigor scales with stakes and structure is added when it reduces error, rework, or ambiguity.
Principle: extensibility follows maturity - remote MCP, plugins, broad tool search, and remote execution are later-phase capabilities gated by stable local SDK integration and Chirality governance.
Principle: domain engines own domain truth - when a domain engine is integrated, Chirality governs interaction, proposals, records, and human gates but does not become the solver.
Principle: fixtures are not core - OpenPipeStress may be the first useful Domain Engine Profile fixture, but its assumptions belong in profile and adapter layers rather than Chirality core runtime.

Working-root selection journey: the app validates that the path exists, is a directory, is readable/writable, and is not inside the instruction root.
Working-root selection journey: the app stores the selected root as local UI state and uses it for file tree, scan, chat session, scaffold, and contract APIs.

Working-root selection acceptance: relative paths are rejected, missing/inaccessible directories show actionable errors, instruction-root conflicts are blocked, and clearing the root disables runtime actions requiring projectRoot.
Agent matrix navigation: selecting a NORMATIVE or EVALUATIVE cell routes to WORKBENCH with agent context; selecting an OPERATIVE cell routes to PIPELINE with category context.
Agent matrix navigation: if deliverables are present, clicking a deliverable row routes to PIPELINE TASK* with that deliverable preselected.
Agent matrix acceptance: disabled or unsupported variants remain visible as coming soon rather than silently disappearing.

Scaffold journey: the app calls POST /api/harness/scaffold and the runtime parses package/deliverable tables, creates tool roots, copies decomposition, writes INIT.md and _Coordination/_COORDINATION.md, creates packages and deliverable folders, and returns validation summaries.

Scaffold acceptance: scaffolding is idempotent for existing directories/files, failures are fail-fast with stage/target-path/created-paths for recovery, and PREPARATION compatibility is reported before the user proceeds.

Workbench persona session journey: the chat panel resolves persona aliases to instruction-file names, the runtime persists turn.accepted before calling the model, streams turn events to the UI, and the user may interrupt the turn.

Workbench persona session acceptance: session identity is preserved across turns for the same root/persona/mode, runtime errors preserve the draft and attachments for retry, interrupt returns a terminal process:exit event, and persisted events can reconstruct accepted turns/deltas/outcome/interruption status.

Operative pipeline journey: the user selects DECOMP, PREP, TASK, or AUDIT, then a category-specific agent or lane; for TASK the user selects scope mode and dynamic scope from the working root, and inspects deliverable status/dependency snapshots applying allowed lifecycle transitions.

Operative pipeline acceptance: deliverable selections reset when project root or scan results become stale, KNOWLEDGE_TYPES mode shows only when a knowledge decomposition marker is detected, and lifecycle transitions enforce authorized actors and approval-SHA requirements for human gate states.

Attachment journey: the UI previews attachments as non-authoritative client metadata, the server validates/classifies/reads attachments, and the turn proceeds if user text exists or at least one valid attachment resolves.
Attachment acceptance: allowed extensions are .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .pdf, .txt, .md, .csv.
Attachment acceptance: symlinks, directories, special files, unsupported extensions, unreadable files, files over 10 MB, and total raw bytes over 18 MB are rejected.
Attachment acceptance: partial attachment failure is non-fatal when executable content remains, and if all attachments fail with empty text the request fails with ATTACHMENT_FAILURE.

API key journey: the user stores a key through Electron IPC, Electron encrypts key material with safeStorage outside the working root, and the server runtime reads the UI key from process global or falls back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

API key acceptance: key material is never written to working-root files, UI key takes precedence over env keys, API key status reports source as ui/env/none, and if secure storage is unavailable the UI reports an error.

Permissioned read tool journey: the runtime resolves the tool pool exposing only permitted read tools, validates input, checks path containment and symlink policy, records the permission decision, executes the tool, stores/summarizes the result, and feeds it back to the model.

Permissioned read tool acceptance: read tool execution appears in both SSE and persisted runtime events, denied/malformed calls do not execute, and large outputs are previewed and stored under session artifacts rather than flooding chat.

Controlled write/edit journey: the runtime exposes write tools only if mode/permission rules allow or can ask, validates target path under working root, rejects instruction-root and (initially) symlink writes, requires exact edit preconditions, requests approval when policy requires ask, and performs atomic write/edit emitting a diff/summary.

Controlled write/edit acceptance: readOnly mode cannot write, dontAsk denies unapproved writes and bash actions, explicit deny rules override session/operator allows, and write/edit operations are auditable through runtime events and project git diffs.

Resume-after-failure journey: when a process is interrupted or fails after input is accepted, runtime event replay shows the accepted turn and terminal failure/cancellation status when the user later opens session history.

Resume-after-failure acceptance: accepted user input is recoverable even if no model token was produced, malformed trailing JSONL writes do not break listing or replay of valid prior events, and session metadata remains usable for listing and resume.

Governed subagent delegation journey: the runtime evaluates evaluateSubagentGovernance as the authoritative gate, requiring environment enablement, persona allowlist, context sealing, pipeline approval, approval reference, and Type 2 task-agent eligibility, and in a later phase creates a child run record with restricted tools/cwd streaming lifecycle to the parent session.

Governed subagent delegation acceptance: delegation without governance metadata is denied, delegation to a non-allowlisted or non-Type-2 candidate is denied, and the parent session records child lifecycle and output artifact path when execution support exists.

Validate-and-package journey: the release operator installs dependencies in frontend/, runs tests/typecheck/harness validation, runs the desktop distribution build, and the build packages app resources and verifies instruction-root integrity.

Validate-and-package acceptance: frontend/dist/Chirality-0.1.0-arm64.dmg is produced for macOS arm64, the app bundle includes expected instruction-root resources, the minimum macOS target is 15.0.0 or later, and the build is unsigned/adhoc by design.

Priority P1 means important for current release quality, governed operation, or runtime maturity.
Priority P2 means desirable, later hardening, or future extension.

FR-002 (P0): the app shall expose working-root selection globally; user can type a path, choose folder in Electron, apply, and clear root.

FR-007 (P0): PORTAL shall render the 3x4 agent matrix using canonical rows NORMATIVE/OPERATIVE/EVALUATIVE and columns GUIDING/APPLYING/JUDGING/REVIEWING.
FR-008 (P0): matrix routing shall follow the docs/SPEC contract - NORMATIVE/EVALUATIVE cells open WORKBENCH and OPERATIVE cells open PIPELINE categories.

FR-011 (P0): PIPELINE shall expose DECOMP, PREP, TASK, and AUDIT category controls, with unsupported options visible and disabled as coming soon.
FR-012 (P0): PIPELINE TASK shall use split selectors for task agent and scope, where scope mode is DELIVERABLES or KNOWLEDGE_TYPES and a target deliverable is required for knowledge-type mode.
FR-013 (P1): dynamic scope scan shall reset invalid selections when the root changes, deliverables are removed, knowledge markers are disabled, or knowledge targets become stale.
FR-014 (P0): the app shall create, list, resume, save, and delete harness sessions; records are stored under .chirality/sessions or CHIRALITY_SESSION_ROOT and filtered by normalized project root.

FR-016 (P0): session boot shall accept runtime options; POST /api/harness/session/boot accepts opts and records boot metadata.
FR-017 (P0): turn execution shall stream Server-Sent Events; POST /api/harness/turn returns text/event-stream with backward-compatible browser-facing events.

FR-019 (P0): users shall be able to interrupt active turns; POST /api/harness/interrupt aborts the active provider request and yields interrupted process:exit.

FR-023 (P0): runtime option fallback chains shall be deterministic - model resolves opts.model -> CHIRALITY_GLOBAL_MODEL or instruction-root frontmatter -> default; tools resolve opts.tools -> persona defaults -> runtime default; max turns resolve opts.maxTurns -> persona defaults -> default.

Internal interface EngineConformanceSuite is the test set any engine adapter, including the first SDK adapter, must pass before becoming the production path.

Internal interface EngineAdapter is the provider-specific translator converting external identifiers, message names, permission modes, tool names, transcript paths, and session IDs into provider-neutral Chirality contracts.
Internal interface TurnEngine is the thin owner for a single harness turn lifecycle around SDK query() through the engine contract.

Internal interface SessionEvents is the append/replay JSONL event API.
Internal interface RunLogger is the redacted structured runtime logger.

Internal interface ChiralityPermissionOverlay implements adapter mode, disallowed tool, hook, explicit hard-deny precedence, and canUseTool policy.

Internal interface ChiralityHooks provides SDK hook callbacks for path containment, instruction-root protection, symlink policy, provenance, failure triage, compaction mirror, and subagent governance.
Internal interface ChiralityMcpTools provides in-process SDK MCP server definitions for deterministic Chirality operations.

Future Domain Engine Profiles may define protected model paths, agent-writable proposal paths, deterministic adapter manifests, operation proposal records, generated summaries, tool result artifacts, and reviewer acceptance records.
Protected domain-engine paths must not be directly mutated by agents; any accepted mutation of domain state must flow through an approved adapter or operation workflow and an explicit human gate.
NFR-001 (P0): no project data shall require external storage; all authoritative state is local files under the working root.

NFR-002 (P0): API keys shall not be written to project files, logs, runtime events, or tool artifacts; key redaction is applied to provider errors and logs and key storage stays under Electron userData.
NFR-003 (P0): renderer outbound traffic shall be allowlisted; non-loopback/non-Anthropic renderer requests are canceled.
NFR-004 (P0): attachment paths shall not follow symlinks; symlink attachments are rejected before provider execution.
NFR-005 (P0): the working root shall not be inside the instruction root; the runtime rejects conflicting root selection.
NFR-006 (P0): runtime tools shall enforce path containment; tool execution cannot read/write outside allowed roots except through explicitly approved policies.
NFR-007 (P0): deny-first permission policy shall be enforced by runtime code; deny rules override all allow decisions.
NFR-028 (P0): SDK settings isolation shall be enforced; the shipped runtime does not load user or local Claude Code settings and tests assert default settingSources: [].

NFR-029 (P0): SDK transcript placement shall be explicit and non-authoritative; the Chirality audit JSONL remains canonical and SDK transcript paths/store keys are recorded preferably under project-controlled runtime folders.
NFR-030 (P0): SDK subprocess packaging shall be verified; the packaged DMG can locate and execute the SDK-bundled Claude Code subprocess without leaking secrets or broadening network policy.
